notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0527.tlg034.1st1K-gr: 38:5 ends with ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπου, 'by man', which sits awkwardly and may be intrusive; whose strength is meant (the wood's or the Lord's) is unclear.

nodes.text: Divinations and omens and dreams are vain, and, as with a woman in labour, your heart has fancies.
Unless they are sent from the Most High as a visitation to you, do not set your heart on them;
For healing comes from the Most High, and from a king he will receive honour.
The skill of a physician will lift up his head, and in the presence of great men he will be admired.
The Lord created medicines out of the earth, and a sensible man will not loathe them.
Was water made sweet by wood, so that its strength might be known by man?
And he gave human beings skill, to be glorified in his marvellous works;
with them he healed and took away his pain.
